setup.pitch: Yearturn burns its old ledger at midnight so the town can begin again. This year somebody burned the unresolved promises too—and the old year refuses to end.
setup.gmSummary: Yearturn's New Year rite closes one civic ledger and opens another. Fulfilled promises are marked complete; unresolved debts and obligations are copied into the new ledger before the old pages are burned. This year council clerk Edrin March, under pressure to make the town look debt-free, ordered the unresolved pages burned without transfer. At midnight the great clock freezes between bells eleven and twelve. The town begins repeating short slices of the final hour, and figures called Yearlings emerge from ash-written promises. The party must recover surviving fragments, identify which obligations were erased, decide whether to restore them, transform them into a public amnesty compact, or break the clock-bound ritual entirely.
setup.background: The ledger tradition began after a corrupt reeve once declared all winter debts erased at midnight while keeping what others owed him. The town created a public carry-forward ceremony so a new year meant renewal without pretending unfinished obligations had vanished. Over centuries this became pageantry. Edrin March wanted Yearturn to announce a clean ledger and attract winter investors. He destroyed the unresolved pages before they were copied. The Old Year is not a god demanding bookkeeping; it is a civic spirit built from repeated public acknowledgment that new beginnings require honest accounting.

quest.objective: Stop the repeating final hour, learn which promises were erased, and decide how Yearturn will enter the new year.
quest.stakes: The town is trapped in escalating time echoes, people are reliving painful moments, and erased obligations could become permanent injustice if the ritual is resolved carelessly.
quest.deadline: TWELFTH BELL: show four chime marks. Fill one after the square, archive, debtor row, and bellworks. When the fourth fills, the clock attempts the final chime and the Old Year manifests.
successConditions: The erased obligations are recovered or reconstructed well enough for a deliberate decision.
The town enters the new year under Restore, Amnesty, or Break.
failureConditions: The party abandons the town after learning the repeating hour is worsening.
The clockworks are destroyed without ending the time echo or accounting for the erased obligations.

facts.text: Unresolved debts and promises are supposed to be copied into the new ledger before the old pages are burned.
Edrin March ordered unresolved pages burned without being copied forward.
The erased entries include wages owed, a bridge repair promise, medical debt, and a winter fuel allotment.
The Old Year is enforcing acknowledgment of unfinished obligations, not demanding that every debt be paid exactly as written.
The town can restore the obligations, replace them with a public amnesty/reparation compact, or break the clock ritual and end supernatural enforcement.

scenes.title: Eleven Again
scenes.purpose: Show the time failure, establish the chime clock, and point the party toward the ledger rather than a generic time curse.
scenes.readAloud: The eleventh bell rings. Confetti rises. Cups lift. Then the same bell rings again. A dropped red scarf jumps from the snow back into a child's hands. The clock's minute hand jerks backward. Around the burn brazier, ash writes one word across the stones: UNFINISHED.
gmNotes: Show four TWELFTH BELL marks. Fill 1/4 when this scene ends.
The loop repeats only short local moments, not the entire adventure.
Mera immediately identifies the ledger rite as the likely source. No check is required to start the investigation.
DC 12 Intelligence (Investigation) on the burn brazier finds UNRESOLVED stamp fragments. Failure still leaves the ash-writing and archive route obvious.
Do not let players spend an hour trying to exploit the time loop before the rules are known; echoes are scene pressure, not unrestricted time travel.

scenes.readAloud: Rows of old ledgers line the archive wall. The new year's book lies open to a beautiful blank page. Beside it, this year's closing schedule has BURN written above COPY in fresh ink. Under the desk, discarded carbon sheets hold ghostly impressions: WAGES. BRIDGE. MEDICAL. FUEL.

The investor letter and Edrin's initials establish intentional alteration without requiring confession.

scenes.title: The Missing Twelfth
scenes.purpose: Expose the last physical evidence and let preparation alter the finale without deciding the moral choice.
scenes.readAloud: The clocktower shakes with every failed chime. Eleven hammer arms rest. The twelfth is locked halfway forward by a bar of blackened paper wound around the gear teeth. Beneath the ash chute sits a bundle of half-burned ledger pages tied with Edrin's council cord.
gmNotes: Fill TWELFTH BELL 4/4 when the twelfth hammer is freed; the finale begins immediately.

DC 13 Dexterity with thieves' tools or Intelligence (Investigation) frees the paper jam safely. Failure deals 1d6 bludgeoning from a snapping gear and still loosens the jam enough for the next attempt to succeed automatically.

Removing the jam does not ring the bell immediately; it opens the path to the upper chamber where the party must choose closure.
If ECHO PRESSURE is 2+, one extra Yearling appears in the finale.

scenes.title: Carry, Forgive, or Cut
scenes.purpose: Resolve the New Year dilemma through honest carry-forward, public amnesty/reparation, or breaking the pact.
scenes.readAloud: The upper chamber has no windows, yet fireworks flash across its walls from moments that have not happened. A circular ledger table stands beneath the bell. Three brass slots are labeled CARRY, FORGIVE, and CUT. Ash rises from the floor into a human shape wearing twelve dim numerals like a crown. “Eleven,” it says. “Not twelve. Name what remains.”
gmNotes: The Old Year starts at 64 HP. Add one Yearling if ECHO PRESSURE is 2+.

CARRY route: place reconstructed obligations into the new ledger and complete 3 Carry actions before 2 failures. Each Action uses DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation/History), Wisdom (Insight), or Charisma (Persuasion) to accurately record terms and responsibility. Failure creates one Yearling or gives an existing Yearling an immediate move; at 2 failures Carry closes but Forgive and Cut remain legal.

FORGIVE route: create a public amnesty/reparation compact at three stations—public obligations, hardship debts, future dispute process. Each station is automatic if the party already secured agreement from affected parties, otherwise DC 13 Charisma (Persuasion) or Wisdom (Insight). Completing all three ends the loop without preserving exact old balances.

CUT route: the clock-bound seal can be targeted after one hostile action or one deliberate rejection of the ledger. AC 14, 18 HP. Destroying it drops the Old Year to 0 HP and permanently ends supernatural ledger enforcement.
Direct combat to 0 HP is legal and has the same consequence as Cut.

Initiative 20: Reprise. One unresolved echo repeats: a creature must succeed on DC 12 Wisdom save or lose 10 feet of movement and cannot take reactions until its next turn as it repeats its last few seconds.

runSteps.text: Any completed route immediately allows the final bell.

scenes.title: Resolution: Written Forward
scenes.purpose: Reward honest carry-forward without pretending every debt is immediately payable.
scenes.readAloud: The twelfth bell rings once. The new ledger is no longer blank. Names, wages, repairs, fuel, and debts stand on its first pages under one heading: UNRESOLVED, NOT FORGOTTEN. Fireworks finally burst outside in the right order.
gmNotes: Award 130 gp total and four Yearturn Favor tokens.
The council must publish carried public obligations quarterly.
Private hardship debts may still be renegotiated later.

scenes.title: Resolution: A Clean Page with Footnotes
scenes.purpose: Reward a structured amnesty that does not erase responsibility.
scenes.readAloud: The final bell rings as old balances are crossed out one by one—but none vanish without a note beside them. WAGES TO BE PAID. BRIDGE TO BE REPAIRED. HARDSHIP LOAN FORGIVEN. FUEL GUARANTEED. The Old Year folds into the margin of the new book like ash pressed into paper.
gmNotes: Award 150 gp total and the New Page Seal, a story item granting advantage on one future Yearturn check involving mediation or public records.
The compact must name how public obligations are repaired even when private hardship debt is forgiven.
Edrin loses sole control of the closing ledger.

scenes.title: Resolution: Midnight Without a Ledger Spirit
scenes.purpose: Respect ending supernatural enforcement while preserving human accountability.
scenes.readAloud: The clock seal snaps. For one breath, every bell in Yearturn is silent. Then a child in the square pulls the public bell rope by hand, and twelve ordinary chimes roll across the roofs. The new ledger is still blank. Mera sets the recovered wage slips on top of it and says, “Magic is gone. Paper is not.”
gmNotes: Award 130 gp total.
The supernatural carry-forward pact ends permanently.
The recovered records still require civic action; destroying the spirit does not erase material obligations.

runSteps.title: Record reward

pathPressure.principle: Prepared reconstruction reduces echo pressure and makes noncombat closure easier, while rushing preserves all endings at higher tactical cost.
prepared: Each reconstructed Debtor Row category removes one local echo and prevents ECHO PRESSURE.
Securing party agreement before the finale can make Forgive stations automatic.
Recovering the ash bundle verifies serial numbers for Carry actions.
rushed: Skipping human records starts the finale with ECHO PRESSURE 2.
Unresolved categories can create additional Yearlings.
Entering without a compact requires checks at each Forgive station.

cutOrder: If 25+ minutes behind, auto-solve the carbon-stack puzzle after one inspection.
If 15+ minutes behind on Debtor Row, combine medical and fuel reconstruction into one scene beat.
Never cut the distinction between acknowledgment and payment or the three finale routes.
optionalOrder: Extended argument with Edrin about investors.
Extra private-debt examples beyond the four required categories.
Historical archive research after the lawful closure options are clear.
